prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept, faithful environment transformation of the supplied approved game concept.
Input image: the game's approved original woodcut concept. It is the visual authority, not a loose inspiration. Transform this composition into chapter four: a BEACH AT NIGHT after leaving a tomb. Preserve the exact scruffy knight's identity, closed bucket helmet, ragged dirty orange cross tabard, short worn sword, wooden shield, proportions, eye treatment and irregular ink line quality.

Create a wide landscape 16:9 concept illustration that reads as a playable 2D side-scroller. The knight stands on the left on a thin horizontal shoreline ground line, facing right. Maintain the reference's generous empty space and hierarchy: bold characters; much lighter, sparse distant landscape. Two opponents on the right, with clear space from the knight: a squat, absurdly ill-tempered barnacle-encrusted crab creature, and a lean ragged sea revenant with a rusty trident, wet seaweed hanging like shabby clothing, small shaded eyes with tiny pale glints. Their sizes and caricature belong to the original rabbit/goblin/skeleton family, not a different fantasy game.

The world behind them: broad dark ocean rendered in spare engraved horizontal lines and a few carved wave curls; a large pale moon left unprinted against a selectively crosshatched charcoal night sky, its reflection made ONLY from broken paper-white horizontal strokes. A low distant craggy island with a very small ruined watchtower; near the far-right horizon an enormous ominous sea-serpent head and a couple of coils rising out of the water, only a distant background landmark, much lighter and simpler than the foreground creatures. Hint at the tomb exit as an old stone opening cut into a low cliff at the extreme left behind the knight. Distinct readable far ocean, middle rocks/surf and near sand layers. Foreground has sparse shells, pebbles, seaweed and a washed-up branch. Complete natural silhouettes, tapered banks and scattered etched ground marks, no square cutoffs, no dense wall of scenery.

Night must feel eerie and moonlit through flat ink density and negative space, NOT through cinematic colored lighting. Exact reference medium: irregular black medieval WOODBLOCK PRINT, fine carved hatching, coarse printed edges, worn ink breaks, aged light parchment, restrained warm ink-grey and leather brown, small dirty pale burnt-orange details. Main parchment family around #E4CCB4/#ECDCC4, ink #24241C; reference-like natural print variations allowed. Keep light paper interiors opaque, especially characters. Match the approved knight's detail and line weight. No yellow cast, no blue/purple palette, no photorealism, no shiny surfaces, no painted gradients, no glossy water or 3D render. Shabby medieval black comedy; unsettling yet a little ridiculous. No gore, no faces on bodies or bellies, no demonic hollow living faces.

Keep the ground approximately 74 percent down the canvas; directly underneath a thin distressed black medieval divider spanning the same width, tiny dirty-orange diamond at its center, exactly the concept's divider language. Below it clean aged parchment with one big elegantly carved black equation: "8 + 7 = ?" with restrained orange inset details like the reference numeral art. No other text, no title, no labels, no HUD, no panels, no cards, no modern buttons. This is one coherent polished concept, not an atlas.
notes: Chapter four after the tomb: return to side view on a moonlit beach.
